answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a shale as the anchor of the cost.
